articles.title: Anti-DDoS Firm Heaped Attacks on Brazilian ISPs
articles.summary: Canvas got pwned by ransomware crew who defaced login pages nationwide, proving that EdTech security is about as robust as cafeteria pizza. When your homework platform becomes someone else's payday, you know we've lost the plot.

articles.title: Help EFF Solve an Issue That's Bigger than Creepy Ads
articles.summary: Microsoft's April patch bonanza fixes 167 vulnerabilities including a SharePoint zero-day and Windows Defender's 'BlueHammer' flaw. AI is apparently better at finding bugs than humans are at writing secure code — shocking absolutely no one.

articles.title: Victory! End-to-End Encrypted RCS Comes to Apple and Android Chats
articles.summary: Instagram quietly murdered its end-to-end encryption feature, breaking years-old promises faster than a Facebook privacy policy update. Meta chose convenience over security, because why protect users when you can just surveil them instead?

articles.title: 'FrostyNeighbor' APT Carefully Targets Govt Orgs in Poland, Ukraine
articles.summary: Cisco's SD-WAN gets skull-fucked by another CVSS 10.0 vulnerability being exploited in the wild. That's two perfect 10s this year — Cisco's really going for the Olympic gold in catastrophic network failures.

articles.title: To gain root access at this company, all an intruder had to do was ask nicely
articles.summary: Linux gets 'Fragnesia' — a kernel memory flaw with public exploit code that hands root access like Halloween candy. The ugly parade of privilege escalation bugs continues, because apparently secure memory handling is still rocket science.

articles.title: Stealer Backdoor Found in 3 Node-IPC Versions Targeting Developer Secrets
articles.summary: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller's authentication bypass (CVE-2026-20182) scores perfect 10.0 and gets actively exploited for admin access. When your network's front door is made of tissue paper, don't act surprised when burglars walk through.

articles.title: ThreatsDay Bulletin: PAN-OS RCE, Mythos cURL Bug, AI Tokenizer Attacks, and 10+ Stories
articles.summary: Supply chain poisoning hits node-ipc package targeting developer secrets — because why hack one target when you can compromise an entire ecosystem? Three malicious versions slipped through, turning dependency management into Russian roulette.

articles.title: Welcome to the vulnpocalypse, as vendors use AI to find bugs and patches multiply like rabbits
articles.summary: BitLocker gets owned by USB stick exploit 'YellowKey' from a disgruntled researcher who went full disclosure. When your disk encryption can be bypassed with a flash drive, maybe it's time to rethink that 'unbreakable' marketing.

articles.title: New BitLocker vulnerability exposes Windows 11 users to system breach
articles.summary: Google confirms first known case of AI-assisted hacking in the wild, because apparently we needed robots to make cybercrime more efficient. The singularity isn't coming — it's already here and it's pwning your infrastructure.

articles.title: Canvas Hack Aftermath: Owner Instructure Reaches Deal With Hacker Group
articles.summary: Foxconn factories got ransacked in cyberattack with Apple, Intel, Google, and NVIDIA files allegedly stolen. When your supply chain partner becomes a data piñata, even the fruit company's secrets aren't safe.
